subject.title: [Refactor] Consolidate synthetic log formats across MCP service pipelines

question: Should OpenClaw Tools and the Codex Supervisor plugin expose one stable cross-service diagnostic format, or should each owner retain service-specific fatal diagnostics over the already-shared transport?
rationale: Source inspection establishes duplication of a small output pattern but not a user-facing compatibility requirement, while the affected implementations now sit on opposite sides of the core/plugin boundary.

options.title: Retain owner-local diagnostics
options.body: Keep the shared stdio transport as-is and allow each service to preserve its own identity and fatal-error wording.

options.title: Define a public diagnostic seam
options.body: Specify a structured cross-service diagnostics contract in an approved plugin SDK/runtime surface, then migrate both callers with focused tests.

recommendation.title: Retain owner-local diagnostics
recommendation.body: Keep the shared stdio transport as-is and allow each service to preserve its own identity and fatal-error wording.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the current OpenClaw Tools MCP bridge and are the strongest history-backed routing candidate for deciding whether its diagnostics are contractual.
